From 95171e45663307fc33a939f0220b39afadfe7cb9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Date: Thu, 14 Dec 2023 18:39:31 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] mei: fix vsc dependency

CONFIG_INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW can be set to built-in even with CONFIG_MEI=m,
but then the driver is not built because Kbuild never enters the
drivers/misc/mei directory for built-in files, leading to a link
failure:

ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_reset" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_init" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_xfer" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_need_read" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_intr_enable" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_intr_synchronize" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_intr_disable" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_register_event_cb" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!

Add an explicit dependency on CONFIG_MEI that was apparently missing,
to ensure the VSC_HW driver cannot be built-in with MEI itself being
a loadable module.

Fixes: 566f5ca97680 ("mei: Add transport driver for IVSC device")
Signed-off-by: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Reviewed-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Wentong Wu <wentong.wu@intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231214183946.109124-1-arnd@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig b/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig
index 858bd701d68c..1e28ca23a74a 100644
--- a/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig
@@ -62,6 +62,7 @@ config INTEL_MEI_GSC
 
 config INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW
 	tristate "Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver"
+	depends on INTEL_MEI
 	depends on ACPI && SPI
 	depends on GPIOLIB || COMPILE_TEST
 	help
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig`**
   - Added a new dependency: `depends on INTEL_MEI` for the configuration option `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW`. This change ensures that the Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver cannot be built as a built-in module if the MEI (Management Engine Interface) itself is configured as a loadable module.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the `Kconfig` file addresses a bug where the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver could be built-in while the `CONFIG_MEI` was set to loadable, leading to undefined references during the linking process. By adding the explicit dependency on `INTEL_MEI`, the patch ensures that the VSC_HW driver can only be built if the MEI driver is also built-in, thus preventing the link failures that were occurring. This change is a direct fix for the issues reported in the error messages related to undefined symbols during the module post-processing stage.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of an explicit dependency in the Kconfig file for the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver on the `INTEL_MEI` configuration. This allowed the VSC_HW driver to be built as a built-in module while the MEI driver was set to be a loadable module, leading to undefined references during the linking process.

Here is the patch:
 config INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW
 	tristate "Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver"
+	depends on INTEL_MEI
 	depends on ACPI && SPI
 	depends on GPIOLIB || COMPILE_TEST

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
config INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW
tristate "Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver"
```
Reason:
The `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver was not explicitly dependent on the `INTEL_MEI` configuration, allowing it to be built as a built-in module while the `MEI` driver could be a loadable module. This mismatch caused undefined references during the linking process, as the VSC_HW driver expected the MEI functions to be available but they were not linked.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	depends on INTEL_MEI
```
Reason:
By adding the explicit dependency on `INTEL_MEI`, the patch ensures that the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver cannot be built-in unless the `MEI` driver is also built-in. This prevents the situation where the VSC_HW driver is built without the necessary MEI functions, thus resolving the undefined reference errors during the linking process.
